## Summary
Patrick Henry profiles four commercial printers (Talient Action Group on Infigo, Calitho on Racad Tech, FrontEnd Graphics on Red Tie Template, Primoprint on an in-house platform) and how each connects their customer-facing W2P storefront to back-end production. Talient is the Infigo data point: CEO Sean Owen on the record about adoption strategy, automation percentages, and the people commitment beyond software cost.

## Key takeaways
- **Talient Action Group hard numbers (2021):** ~26% of incoming Infigo storefront orders go direct to press in an automated workflow. Goal: 60%. The remaining 74% are vetted by CSR / prepress before release.
- **Pandemic onboarding velocity:** Talient added 26 new W2P customers in 2020 (~2/month). Owen attributes this primarily to clients wanting decentralized buying and variable-data tooling — not just contact avoidance.
- **Automation savings per job:** 8–12 minutes/job production time on automated W2P orders vs. manual entry. Also drives better inventory forecasting / buying power.
- **Catalog size:** ~700 ready-to-order items across Talient's storefronts at time of writing — the "supermarket shelf" that pulls smaller accounts onto self-service.
- **Owen's deployment warning (quoted):** "The commitment is definitely more than just the cost of a Web-to-storefront platform or software. The commitment really is in the people you have around you, and whether they have the skill set to change the way you sell the customers and service them." Employees must be prepared to "disrupt" current workflows; running W2P as a bolt-on to legacy order entry forfeits the printer-side benefits.
- **Vendor-selection lens (Taheripour @ Calitho):** Most vendors at similar price points have similar capabilities — evaluate on support responsiveness, integration ability, and how fast they ship feature requests / bug fixes. SaaS over self-hosted for new entrants.
- **Front-end "tooling" matters:** Storefront/portal design is compared to a diecutter — "if we cut corners on the initial build, we will pay for it down the line." Resonates with the deeper-than-it-looks setup cost of an Infigo product/template.
